2608.07316.title: Natural Language Processing Psychometrics
2608.07316.paper_summary: Natural Language Processing (NLP) models predicting mental health outcomes rarely specify what they measure: contextual knowledge, emotional content, or syntactic structure. NLP Psychometrics treats psychological prediction from text as a psychometric problem, linking scores to interpretable linguistic evidence and testing beyond the training text format. Nine LLMs, conditioned on controlled personas (cognitive digital shadows), completed psychometric questionnaires with textual explanations per item. We extracted emotional profiles and syntactic-semantic structure via textual forma mentis networks, combined with personality and sociodemographic variables in ablated random forest (RF) regressors, using SHAP to identify which features drove performance and in which direction. Full RF models explained up to 70.8% of variance in life satisfaction (SWLS), 55.7% in depression (PHQ-9), and, for DASS-21, 68.5% depression, 76.0% anxiety, 72.4% stress. Sociodemographics alone explained no meaningful variance in depression, anxiety, or stress, but did so for life satisfaction, where emotion features and income were the strongest predictors; neuroticism and network topology instead dominated depression and anxiety, reversing direction between them. Without retraining, RF models separated diaries from low- and high-score personas ($r$ up to 0.91) and, using only network/emotion features, classified clinical from control participants in real transcripts with up to 68% accuracy. These results show the promise and limits of synthetic data: LLM personas can expose model biases, recover patterns consistent with clinical rumination, and support psychometric prediction from human text without a matched questionnaire, but cannot substitute for human validation. NLP Psychometrics makes these distinctions explicit, measurable, and testable through interpretable AI and network/emotional features.
2608.07316.paper_summary_zh: 自然語言處理（NLP）模型預測心理健康結果時，鮮少明確說明其測量內容：上下文知識、情感內容或句法結構。NLP心理測量將文本中的心理預測視為一個心理測量問題，將分數與可解釋的語言證據聯繫起來，並在超越訓練文本格式的情況下進行測試。九個大型語言模型（LLMs），基於受控的人格（認知數位影子），完成了帶有每個項目文本解釋的心理測量問卷。我們通過文本形式思維網絡提取情感輪廓和句法-語義結構，並結合個性和社會人口變數，使用消融隨機森林（RF）回歸模型，利用SHAP識別哪些特徵驅動了性能及其方向。完整的RF模型解釋了高達70.8%的生活滿意度變異（SWLS）、55.7%的抑鬱（PHQ-9），以及DASS-21中68.5%的抑鬱、76.0%的焦慮和72.4%的壓力。僅社會人口學變數對抑鬱、焦慮或壓力未解釋出有意義的變異，但對生活滿意度卻有解釋，其中情感特徵和收入是最強的預測因子；神經質和網絡拓撲則主導了抑鬱和焦慮，兩者之間的方向相反。在不重新訓練的情況下，RF模型將低分和高分人格的日記分開（$r$高達0.91），並僅使用網絡/情感特徵，在真實文本中將臨床參與者與對照參與者分類，準確率高達68%。這些結果顯示了合成數據的潛力和限制：LLM人格可以揭示模型偏見，恢復與臨床沉思一致的模式，並支持從人類文本進行心理測量預測，而無需匹配的問卷，但無法替代人類驗證。NLP心理測量使這些區別變得明確、可測量且可通過可解釋的AI和網絡/情感特徵進行測試。
